key_insight: SANA-Video 2.0 shows that high-quality video generation can be achieved with a hybrid attention design that keeps the long-sequence efficiency of linear attention while approaching the quality of full softmax models. It scales to 5B and 14B parameters and can generate up to 720p video on a single GPU.
problem_solved: Video diffusion transformers are often expensive because full softmax attention scales quadratically with sequence length, making high-resolution and long-video generation hard to run efficiently. This paper addresses the tradeoff between quality and efficiency in video generation.
method: Uses a unified hybrid video diffusion transformer architecture at 5B and 14B scales.
Combines gated linear attention for efficient O(N)-dominated token mixing with periodic gated-softmax anchors to preserve quality.
Introduces attention residuals to support stable information flow without relying on quadratic attention throughout the model.
impact: For AI practitioners, this means stronger video generation models that are more practical to deploy on limited hardware, including single-GPU setups. It offers a path toward longer, higher-resolution video synthesis without the usual compute cost explosion.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of linear attention vs full softmax attention complexity
Architecture diagram showing gated linear attention and periodic softmax anchors
Performance tradeoff chart comparing quality, resolution, and compute usage
paper_title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
paper_authors: Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Yitong Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu
